title: CRUD service boundaries
summary: A backend pattern that keeps transport, validation, business rules, and persistence independently testable.
overview: A CRUD feature is most reusable when HTTP concerns stop at the controller and persistence details stop at the repository boundary.

sections.heading: Flow
sections.body: Controller → application service → repository. Domain decisions belong in the application service; request parsing and response codes belong in the controller.

sections.heading: Contract first
sections.body: Define the smallest repository interface the use case needs. This makes the logic portable across MongoDB, SQL, or an in-memory test double.

sections.heading: Validate at the boundary
sections.body: Treat transport input as untrusted. Validate shape and primitive constraints before calling the application service, then enforce business invariants inside the service where every transport can share them.

sections.heading: Map errors intentionally
sections.body: Domain and application errors should not know about HTTP. Translate known errors at the controller or an exception-filter boundary, and avoid leaking database error messages to callers.

sections.heading: Test through ports
sections.body: Exercise application behavior with an in-memory repository that implements the same contract. Keep separate integration tests for the real persistence adapter and a small end-to-end test for transport mapping.
